title: Concept Drills — Fundamental Principles of Organic Chemistry (Class 11 Chemistry)
subject: chemistry

questions.question: Why does chloroacetic acid (ClCH₂COOH) stronger than acetic acid? Name the effect.
questions.solution: The −I effect: Cl withdraws electron density through σ bonds, pulling electron density away from the carboxylate anion and dispersing its negative charge — the conjugate base is stabilised, so the acid is stronger. Inductive effects are transmitted through σ bonds and fade with distance.

questions.question: Is the carbonate ion 'switching' between three structures? What does resonance actually mean?
questions.solution: No — the real ion is a single structure that is a HYBRID of the resonance forms: the two negative charges are spread equally over three oxygens (each bond 1⅓ order). Resonance forms are bookkeeping, not flickering states. Evidence: all three C–O bonds are identical in length — between single and double.

questions.question: Explain the stability order 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺ for carbocations using two effects.
questions.solution: (1) HYPERCONJUGATION: adjacent C–H σ bonds overlap with the empty p orbital, delocalising the charge — more alkyl groups give more hyperconjugative structures. (2) INDUCTIVE: alkyl groups donate (+I), dispersing the positive charge. Both effects grow with alkyl substitution, so tertiary cations are most stabilised — hence SN1 rates follow the same order.

questions.question: How does the electromeric effect differ from resonance, and why does it matter in addition reactions?
questions.solution: Electromeric effect is a COMPLETE, TEMPORARY shift of a π electron pair to one atom under the attack of a reagent (E effect) — it exists only while the attacking species is present. Resonance is a permanent delocalisation. In C=C addition, the reagent's approach polarises the π bond (electromeric), generating the carbocation that the second part of the reagent then attacks.

questions.question: Why do organic reactions generally proceed more slowly than ionic ones like AgNO₃ + NaCl?
questions.solution: Ionic reactions are instant — oppositely charged ions just meet. Organic reactions require breaking COVALENT bonds, which means climbing an activation-energy barrier: bonds must stretch, reorganise, sometimes pass through high-energy intermediates (carbocations, radicals). Covalent reorganisation costs energy; ionic combination does not.
